intro: You've searched for a "self assessment accountant near me", so you're likely looking for someone local to help you file your Self Assessment tax return without the stress. Whether you're self-employed, a landlord or have untaxed income, a good accountant can make sure everything is correct and filed on time. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK accountant who will quote you directly, with no obligation.
need_heading: What people searching for a local Self Assessment accountant usually need
need_lead: Most people want a straightforward, local expert who can take the worry out of their tax return.
needs: You're self-employed and need to file your first Self Assessment return but aren't sure what expenses you can claim.
You rent out a property and have to declare the rental income, but the rules on allowable expenses and reliefs confuse you.
You're a company director with dividend income or benefits in kind that need to be included on your personal tax return.
You've received a letter from HMRC about a late filing penalty or an enquiry, and you want professional help to sort it out.
You've changed jobs or started a side hustle and now have untaxed income that needs to be declared through Self Assessment.
context_heading: What to understand about Self Assessment and finding an accountant
context: Self Assessment returns for a tax year are due online by the end of January the following year. Filing early gives you and your accountant time to check claims and reliefs properly, and to understand how payments on account might affect your cash flow.

In the UK, "accountant" is not a protected title, so anyone can call themselves one. Look for protected titles like Chartered Accountant or Chartered Certified Accountant, and ask which professional body supervises the firm for anti-money-laundering purposes.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Explain why you need a Self Assessment accountant, for example whether you're newly self-employed, a landlord, or have untaxed income.
Mention if you've already received a notice to file from HMRC or if you're filing for the first time.
Say whether you need help with a specific tax year or ongoing support.
Include your approximate income sources and any complexity, such as multiple properties or foreign income.
Let us know if you have a deadline coming up or have already missed one.
Tell us your preferred location or whether you're happy to work remotely.
questions: Are you supervised by a professional body for anti-money-laundering purposes, and which one?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How do you handle complaints if I'm unhappy with your service?
What information will you need from me to prepare my Self Assessment return?
How will payments on account affect my cash flow, and when will I need to pay them?
What are your fees, and how are they structured?

faqs.q: Do I need an accountant for Self Assessment?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but an accountant can help if your affairs are complex, if you're unsure about expenses or reliefs, or if you want to avoid mistakes and penalties. They can also advise on payments on account and cash flow.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for filing my Self Assessment return?
faqs.a: The online filing deadline is the end of January after the tax year ends. If you're filing for the first time, you need to register with HMRC in good time.

faqs.q: How do I check an accountant's credentials?
faqs.a: Look for protected titles such as Chartered Accountant or Chartered Certified Accountant, and ask which professional body supervises the firm for anti-money-laundering purposes. It's also reasonable to ask about professional indemnity insurance and complaints procedures.

faqs.q: Can you help me find a local accountant?
faqs.a: Yes, iComply introduces you to a suitable UK accountant based on your needs. They will then quote you directly, and you can decide whether to proceed.
